Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
The issue is caused by an infinite loop in the wrapping code of the `HelpFormatter` class. When there is not enough space to display a word on a single line, the `printWrapped` method is called repeatedly without proper handling, leading to the infinite loop and eventual JVM crash with an OutOfMemoryError.

Here is the step-by-step breakdown of the issue:
1. The test case creates an `Options` object and adds an option with a long description.
2. The `testInfiniteLoop` method of the test case creates a `HelpFormatter` object, sets the width to 20, and then calls `formatter.printHelp("app", options);`.
3. The `printHelp` method of the `HelpFormatter` class prints the usage, header, options, and footer. When it encounters a long description that does not fit within the specified width, it calls the `printWrapped` method to wrap the text.
4. The `printWrapped` method calls itself recursively without proper termination conditions, leading to an infinite loop when trying to wrap the long description text.

To fix this issue, we need to ensure that the `printWrapped` method has proper termination conditions to prevent infinite recursion. A termination condition based on the length of the text being wrapped or the available width should be added to stop the recursion when necessary.

The methods that need to be fixed are:
1. `org.apache.commons.cli.HelpFormatter.printWrapped(java.io.PrintWriter, int, java.lang.String)`
2. Potentially `org.apache.commons.cli.HelpFormatter.printHelp(java.io.PrintWriter, int, java.lang.String, java.lang.String, org.apache.commons.cli.Options, int, int, java.lang.String, boolean)` as it may need additional checks to prevent the infinite loop.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).

```
org.apache.commons.cli.HelpFormatter.printWrapped(java.io.PrintWriter, int, java.lang.String)
org.apache.commons.cli.HelpFormatter.printHelp(java.io.PrintWriter, int, java.lang.String, java.lang.String, org.apache.commons.cli.Options, int, int, java.lang.String, boolean)
```
